P1.title: Three Ways Up
P1.prompt: Choose a launch. Reliability, mass and orbit travel together.

choices.label: Reliable rideshare
choices.detail: 500 km; 6 kg cap. The rocket decides the orbit.

choices.label: Dedicated launch
choices.detail: 600 km; more freedom, higher price.

choices.label: Budget low-orbit launch
choices.detail: 300 km saves money, but life falls below two years.

P1.hint: Keep total spacecraft mass below the launch and bus limits.

P2.title: Orbit Ring
P2.prompt: Dedicated launches can choose orbit. Rideshare keeps its assigned orbit.

choices.label: Sarawak coverage
choices.detail: Keep the safe coverage window.

choices.label: Low orbit
choices.detail: Dedicated only: less drag margin and shorter life.

choices.label: High orbit
choices.detail: Dedicated only: longer life, smaller images.

P2.hint: Rideshare orbit is fixed. Change P1 for an independent orbit.

P3.title: Surprise Jar
P3.prompt: Leave room for surprises inside 2.5 million.

choices.label: Keep a reserve
choices.detail: Save 0.20 M of headroom.

choices.label: Spend the reserve
choices.detail: Extra planning buys a little science.

choices.label: Large reserve
choices.detail: Keep 0.40 M free; use simpler hardware.

E1.title: The Frame
E1.prompt: Fit the bus around the forest imager.

choices.label: 6U frame
choices.detail: Balanced 6 kg bus.

choices.label: 3U frame
choices.detail: Cheaper, but the 4 kg bus fills quickly.

choices.label: 12U frame
choices.detail: Room for extras; costs more.

E2.title: Sun Test
E2.prompt: Solar power must run the spacecraft and refill the battery.

choices.label: Deployable solar
choices.detail: 28 W total generation.

choices.label: Body panels
choices.detail: 18 W total: little charging margin.

choices.label: Large solar
choices.detail: 38 W total; heavier and dearer.

E3.title: The Dark Box
E3.prompt: Survive 35 minutes of shadow. Refill before the next eclipse.

choices.label: 40 Wh battery
choices.detail: Carries about 20 W with a reserve.

choices.label: 20 Wh battery
choices.detail: Small pack; a high payload load can exhaust it.

choices.label: 60 Wh battery
choices.detail: Comfortable night margin, more mass.

E3.hint: A 35-minute eclipse uses load × 35/60 Wh. Leave a reserve.

E4.title: Thruster Shelf
E4.prompt: Thrusters are insurance against crowded space.

choices.label: Fit thrusters
choices.detail: Give the satellite a way to step aside.

choices.label: No thrusters
choices.detail: Save money and mass; a debris hit can end the mission.

E5.title: Weigh-In
E5.prompt: Weigh it twice. Choose your mass margin.

choices.label: Trim the brackets
choices.detail: Remove 0.20 kg safely.

choices.label: Keep standard hardware
choices.detail: No extra trimming cost.

choices.label: Rush lightweight parts
choices.detail: Save more mass but lose three months.

C1.title: Radio Bench
C1.prompt: Choose a radio that can send the images home.

choices.label: S-band
choices.detail: Balanced power and data.

choices.label: X-band
choices.detail: Faster, heavier and more demanding.

choices.label: Ka-band
choices.detail: Fastest, but rain fades the signal.

C2.title: Wall Map
C2.prompt: Kuching is home. Add a backup dish if you can.

choices.label: Kuching plus backup
choices.detail: A second station protects missed passes.

choices.label: Kuching only
choices.detail: Cheaper; outages and rain cost more data.

choices.label: Global network
choices.detail: Excellent coverage at a higher price.

C3.title: Pass Timeline
C3.prompt: Place downlinks inside visible passes. Keep the data tank from overflowing.

choices.label: Balanced passes
choices.detail: Room for forest images and retry passes.

choices.label: Maximum imaging
choices.detail: Fill the tank faster than the radio can empty it.

choices.label: Extra downlinks
choices.detail: More delivered data, less time to image.

C3.hint: Schedule downlinks before storage fills; keep at least 70% returned.

S1.title: Magic Eye
S1.prompt: Healthy leaf, dry leaf. The imager sees the difference.

choices.label: Forest imager
choices.detail: Required primary instrument.

choices.label: Remove the imager
choices.detail: Saves resources but fails the forest mission.

S2.title: Instrument Shelf
S2.prompt: Pack useful instruments. Watch mass and power.

choices.label: Thermal sensor
choices.detail: See through some cloud. Adds 6 W.

choices.label: No add-on
choices.detail: Keep the mission simple.

choices.label: Second imager
choices.detail: More science, heavier and power hungry.

choices.label: Full instrument rack
choices.detail: Ambitious: 14 W extra can break the power budget.

S2.hint: Thermal needs 6 W. Keep both mass and power gauges green.

S3.title: Frame the Shot
S3.prompt: Wide is coarse. Narrow is sharp. Avoid cloud.

choices.label: Wide forest survey
choices.detail: Cover Sarawak regularly.

choices.label: Narrow detail
choices.detail: Sharp images, fewer locations and more data.

choices.label: Off-target demonstration
choices.detail: A beautiful view outside the required region.

S4.title: Cloud Calendar
S4.prompt: Put imaging slots in clearer months. Respect power and data caps.

choices.label: Clear-month plan
choices.detail: Time forest observations around local weather.

choices.label: Image every pass
choices.detail: More data than the radio can carry.

choices.label: Few safe observations
choices.detail: Easy downlinks, smaller science return.

R1.title: Power vs Science
R1.prompt: Thermal adds 6 W. Keep enough power to recharge after eclipse.

choices.label: Stagger the loads
choices.detail: Run high-power instruments at different times.

choices.label: Run everything
choices.detail: Gain science at a power cost.

choices.label: Add charging margin
choices.detail: More solar hardware.

R2.title: Mass vs Comms
R2.prompt: The radio shares the launch mass limit with every other part.

choices.label: Share the margin
choices.detail: Trim the mounting plate.

choices.label: Keep all extras
choices.detail: No change; check the mass gauge.

choices.label: Larger adapter
choices.detail: Adds structure, cost and one month.

R3.title: Data vs Comms / EV7
R3.prompt: Science requests a second imager. Negotiate a plan the radio can support.

choices.label: Prioritize useful images
choices.detail: Protect downlinks and keep the primary instrument.

choices.label: Accept second-imager request
choices.detail: More science, power, mass and data demand.

choices.label: Buy more passes
choices.detail: Return more data at higher cost.

P4.title: What Comes First?
P4.prompt: Place the token: Science, Safety or Cost. No wrong answer; a different mission.

choices.label: Safety
choices.detail: Keep healthy operating margins.

choices.label: Science
choices.detail: Chase more forest measurements.

choices.label: Cost
choices.detail: Keep resources for the next team.

P5.title: T-Minus
P5.prompt: Check power, battery, antenna, instruments, mass, orbit, budget and schedule.

choices.label: Go
choices.detail: Proceed when every requirement is green.

choices.label: Hold one month
choices.detail: Use the month to reduce load and improve reliability.

P5.hint: A hold cannot remove a hard requirement. Revise the relevant department choice.

EV8.title: Q2 · Heavy Clouds

choices.label: Switch sensors
choices.detail: Use thermal if fitted; otherwise wait for a clear pass.

choices.label: Keep optical imaging
choices.detail: Cloud reduces the science return.

EV8.hint: Thermal is useful when the optical view is cloudy.

EV6.title: Q3 · Station Outage

choices.label: Reroute the pass
choices.detail: Use the backup dish or recover on the next pass.

choices.label: Wait at Kuching
choices.detail: Lose downlink time.

EV6.hint: A backup station preserves more of this quarter’s data.

C4.title: Q4 · Rain at the Dish
C4.prompt: Rain is coming. Watch the needle!

choices.label: Adapt the downlink
choices.detail: Track the signal and slow down when rain grows.

choices.label: Hold maximum rate
choices.detail: Rain can corrupt the data.

C4.hint: Keep the needle green. Ka-band is most sensitive to rain.

EV3.title: Q5 · Long Eclipse
EV3.prompt: Protect the battery through a longer night.

choices.label: Triage the loads
choices.detail: Pause science to protect the spacecraft.

choices.label: Keep all instruments on
choices.detail: A small battery may run flat.

EV3.hint: Switch off science loads before the battery reaches zero.

EV9.title: Q6 · Instrument Glitch
EV9.prompt: Repeat the reset sequence and recover the forest imager.

choices.label: Reset carefully
choices.detail: Recover the instrument in order.

choices.label: Skip the reset
choices.detail: Lose science and spacecraft health.

EV9.hint: Read the pattern before pressing the buttons.

EV5.title: Q7 · Debris Warning
EV5.prompt: Steer away for twenty seconds. No thrusters means no evasive burn.

choices.label: Avoid the debris
choices.detail: Thrusters can change the orbit; otherwise track the near miss.

choices.label: Continue observations
choices.detail: Save science time but increase collision risk.

EV5.hint: Move into clear space early. Thrusters are insurance.

EV4.title: Q8 · Battery Heating
EV4.prompt: Drag loads off. Stay under the red line.

choices.label: Cool down
choices.detail: Shed payload load and protect the battery.

choices.label: Keep full power
choices.detail: Heat shortens battery life.

EV4.hint: Reduce payload load before the temperature reaches red.
